86: class RateLimiter:
87:     """Sliding-window limiter: at most `limit` requests per `window` seconds,
88:     per key (source IP here). Replaces the previous fixed-window scheme
89:     which allowed a brief double-rate burst at the window boundary (up to
90:     2*limit in one window's worth of time straddling two fixed windows).
91:     Sliding window prunes timestamps older than `window` on every `allow()`
92:     and counts only those still inside the window. Not built for distributed
93:     scale -- enough to bound abuse against a single small process, which is
94:     the actual deployment this is for. Applied to every endpoint, not just
95:     /report: unauthenticated attempts against /banned or /ban are exactly
96:     the kind of thing worth throttling too (ID enumeration, admin-key
97:     brute-forcing), not just report flooding.
98:     `max_keys` is a hard cap on distinct keys held at once, evicting the
99:     least-recently-seen key when exceeded. `_prune()` alone only runs
100:     roughly once per `window` seconds, so a burst of distinct source IPs
101:     within one window grew `_hits` without bound until the next prune
102:     (#25) -- this cap bounds memory independently of that timer."""
103: 
104:     DEFAULT_MAX_KEYS = 4096
105: 
106:     def __init__(self, limit, window, max_keys=DEFAULT_MAX_KEYS):
107:         # isinstance(True, int) is True, so bool needs its own carve-out:
108:         # True == 1 would otherwise silently cap the table at one bucket.
109:         # Floats are rejected outright too -- inf/nan sail past a `< 1`
110:         # check and then make `len(...) >= max_keys` permanently False,
111:         # reopening the unbounded growth this cap exists to close (#25).
112:         if isinstance(max_keys, bool) or not isinstance(max_keys, int) or max_keys < 1:
113:             raise ValueError("max_keys must be a positive integer")
114:         self.limit = limit
115:         self.window = window
116:         self.max_keys = max_keys
117:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
118:         self._hits = {}  # key -> deque[monotonic timestamps], LRU-ordered
119:         self._buckets = self._hits  # compat alias for older tests inspecting _buckets
120:         self._last_prune = time.monotonic()
121: 
122:     def allow(self, key):
123:         now = time.monotonic()
124:         with self._lock:
125:             dq = self._hits.get(key)
126:             if dq is None:
127:                 if len(self._hits) >= self.max_keys:
128:                     # Evict the least-recently-seen key, not the caller:
129:                     # a distinct-IP flood then only churns its own buckets
130:                     # instead of growing memory, and an evicted legitimate
131:                     # key restarts with a fresh (generous, not punitive)
132:                     # budget on its next request.
133:                     self._hits.pop(next(iter(self._hits)))
134:                 dq = collections.deque()
135:                 self._hits[key] = dq
136:             else:
137:                 # Mark recently seen so eviction above drops the
138:                 # least-recently-seen key (pop + reinsert moves a plain
139:                 # dict's key to the end; reassigning alone would not).
140:                 self._hits[key] = self._hits.pop(key)
141:                 dq = self._hits[key]
142:             # prune outside window
143:             while dq and now - dq[0] >= self.window:
144:                 dq.popleft()
145:             if len(dq) >= self.limit:
146:                 # still need occasional prune of stale keys even on deny
147:                 if now - self._last_prune >= self.window:
148:                     self._prune(now)
149:                 return False
150:             dq.append(now)
151:             if now - self._last_prune >= self.window:
152:                 self._prune(now)
153:             return True
154: 
155:     def _prune(self, now):
156:         """Drop keys whose deque is empty or whose newest entry is already
157:         outside the window. Keeps _hits bounded in a long-running process
158:         with many distinct source IPs, same purpose as before but adapted
159:         to deque storage."""
160:         stale = [k for k, dq in self._hits.items()
161:                  if not dq or now - dq[-1] >= self.window]
162:         for k in stale:
163:             del self._hits[k]
164:         self._last_prune = now

238: class BoundedThreadingMixIn(socketserver.ThreadingMixIn):
239:     """Cap concurrent handler threads so a burst of slow-trickling
240:     connections can't unboundedly grow the thread count (#100).
241: 
242:     ThreadingHTTPServer spawns one OS thread per accepted connection with
243:     no cap: each connection already has a per-read `timeout` plus an
244:     absolute CONNECTION_DEADLINE_SEC watchdog, but a client opening many
245:     connections at once and trickling bytes just under those bounds can
246:     still force one thread per connection for the full deadline window.
247:     Bounding here also bounds clean-shutdown latency, since
248:     daemon_threads=False makes server_close() join every handler thread.
249: 
250:     Rejects excess connections with an immediate 503 + close instead of
251:     queueing: queueing in the accept loop would stall legitimate clients
252:     behind attacker-held slots, and the daemon client already retries
253:     report POSTs. The semaphore is per-server-instance (created in
254:     __init__, before any accept loop runs), so separate test instances
255:     in the same process don't share a budget."""
256: 
257:     # Longest the accept loop ever waits between overload log lines: the
258:     # rejection log below is rate-limited to at most one synchronous
259:     # stderr write per interval so a flood of over-capacity connections
260:     # can't park the accept loop behind a backpressured log sink.
261:     OVERLOAD_LOG_INTERVAL_SEC = 5.0
262: 
263:     def __init__(self, *args, max_connections=DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS,
264:                  **kwargs):
265:         self._conn_semaphore = threading.Semaphore(max_connections)
266:         self.max_connections = max_connections
267:         self._overload_log_lock = threading.Lock()
268:         self._overload_log_last = 0.0
269:         self._overload_log_suppressed = 0
270:         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
271: 
272:     def process_request(self, request, client_address):
273:         # Non-blocking: never park the accept loop behind attacker-held
274:         # slots. An accepted-but-unhandled connection still holds its fd,
275:         # so prompt close (not a wait with timeout) is what actually
276:         # bounds fd/thread pressure under a many-connection burst.
277:         if not self._conn_semaphore.acquire(blocking=False):
278:             # Over-capacity rejections used to be silent server-side: the
279:             # client got its 503 below, but stderr showed nothing, so an
280:             # operator watching logs couldn't tell a rejection burst apart
281:             # from a quiet server (#30). Throttled to one line per
282:             # OVERLOAD_LOG_INTERVAL_SEC (with a suppressed count) so a
283:             # rejection flood can't stall the accept loop behind a
284:             # backpressured stderr -- the 503 itself is still sent per
285:             # connection, only the log line is coalesced.
286:             self._log_overload_rejection(client_address)
287:             self._reject_overloaded(request)
288:             return
289:         try:
290:             super().process_request(request, client_address)
291:         except Exception:
292:             # ThreadingMixIn.process_request() spawns a thread and start()
293:             # itself can raise (thread/resource limit): then
294:             # process_request_thread() never runs, so its finally-release
295:             # never fires. Release here and re-raise so the caller's
296:             # handle_error/shutdown_request path still runs -- otherwise
297:             # repeated failures leak the semaphore to zero and every later
298:             # connection gets 503 even after load drops.
299:             self._conn_semaphore.release()
300:             raise
301: 
302:     def process_request_thread(self, request, client_address):
303:         try:
304:             super().process_request_thread(request, client_address)
305:         finally:
306:             # Released even if finish_request() raises: handle_error() is
307:             # inside ThreadingMixIn.process_request_thread, but a bug in
308:             # shutdown_request() itself must still not leak a slot forever.
309:             self._conn_semaphore.release()
310: 
311:     def _log_overload_rejection(self, client_address):
312:         # At most one stderr write per OVERLOAD_LOG_INTERVAL_SEC: the
313:         # accept loop runs process_request() inline, so one blocking
314:         # write per rejected connection would let a rejection flood (or
315:         # a backpressured log sink) stall legitimate accepts. Rejections
316:         # inside the window only bump a counter, folded into the next
317:         # emitted line. getattr defaults keep __new__-built test
318:         # instances (which skip __init__) working.
319:         now = time.monotonic()
320:         lock = getattr(self, "_overload_log_lock", None)
321:         if lock is None:
322:             lock = self._overload_log_lock = threading.Lock()
323:             self._overload_log_last = 0.0
324:             self._overload_log_suppressed = 0
325:         with lock:
326:             last = self._overload_log_last
327:             if now - last < self.OVERLOAD_LOG_INTERVAL_SEC:
328:                 self._overload_log_suppressed += 1
329:                 return
330:             self._overload_log_last = now
331:             suppressed, self._overload_log_suppressed = (
332:                 self._overload_log_suppressed, 0)
333:         suffix = (
334:             " (+%d similar suppressed in last %.0fs)"
335:             % (suppressed, self.OVERLOAD_LOG_INTERVAL_SEC) if suppressed else ""
336:         )
337:         sys.stderr.write(
338:             "ac_server: connection from %r rejected: over "
339:             "--max-connections (%d)%s\n"
340:             % (client_address, self.max_connections, suffix)
341:         )

343:     def _reject_overloaded(self, request):
344:         # Best-effort 503 so a legitimate daemon bursting past the cap
345:         # gets a retryable signal instead of a bare reset; failures here
346:         # (peer already gone, unix-socket edge) just fall through to the
347:         # close -- the point is bounding, not the status line.
348:         try:
349:             request.settimeout(2)
350:             body = b'{"error": "server busy"}'
351:             request.sendall(
352:                 b"HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\r\n"
353:                 b"Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
354:                 b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode("ascii")
355:                 + b"\r\nConnection: close\r\nRetry-After: 5\r\n\r\n"
356:                 + body

358:         except OSError:
359:             pass
360:         finally:
361:             # shutdown(SHUT_WR) before close: closing a socket with unread
362:             # request bytes still queued can RST and discard the 503 we
363:             # just sent. shutdown_request() does the SHUT_WR-then-close
364:             # sequence so the client actually receives the retryable
365:             # response.
366:             try:
367:                 self.shutdown_request(request)
368:             except OSError:
369:                 pass

588: class Store:
589:     """One SQLite connection per request (see handler) -- simplest way to
590:     be correct under ThreadingHTTPServer without sharing a connection
591:     across threads."""

593:     # SQLite schema version, tracked via PRAGMA user_version (#30: the
594:     # server previously had no schema-migration/versioning story at all).
595:     # Fresh DBs are stamped with this; pre-existing version-0 DBs (every
596:     # DB created before this existed) are stamped on open since their
597:     # tables already match version 1. Anything else is a newer/unknown
598:     # schema this code doesn't understand -- fail closed rather than
599:     # writing into it.
600:     SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

602:     def __init__(self, db_path, max_reports_per_client=1000,
603:                  max_total_reports=100000, vacuum_interval=1000):
604:         self.db_path = db_path
605:         # Fail closed on a symlinked DB path (#30): sqlite3.connect()
606:         # follows symlinks, so a pre-planted link would redirect every
607:         # report/ban read and write (and the _ensure_private chmod below)
608:         # at an attacker-chosen target. Only the final component is
609:         # checked -- a symlinked parent dir (e.g. /tmp -> /private/tmp)
610:         # is a normal configuration, not an attack. The check races a
611:         # concurrent swap between lstat and connect when the DB dir is
612:         # writable by someone else; the deployment expectation (same as
613:         # the --unix-socket dir rule) is an operator-owned dir.
614:         try:
615:             st = os.lstat(db_path)
616:         except FileNotFoundError:
617:             pass
618:         else:
619:             if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
620:                 raise RuntimeError(
621:                     "ac_server: --db path %r is a symlink -- refusing to "
622:                     "open it (point --db at the real file)" % (db_path,)
623:                 )
624:         # Bounds how many rows a single client_id can hold in `reports`,
625:         # trimmed on every insert (see add_report). Without this, a single
626:         # spammy or misbehaving daemon has no limit on how much it can grow
627:         # the SQLite file, since `list_reports`'s LIMIT only bounds what a
628:         # query returns, not what accumulates on disk (#60). 0/None disables
629:         # the cap.
630:         self.max_reports_per_client = max_reports_per_client
631:         # Bounds how many rows the whole `reports` table can hold across
632:         # ALL client_ids, trimmed on every insert right after the
633:         # per-client trim above (see add_report). The per-client cap alone
634:         # can't do this: anyone able to mint arbitrarily many distinct
635:         # client_ids grows the SQLite file without bound (#26). Oldest
636:         # rows go first, same as the per-client trim. 0/None disables
637:         # the cap.
638:         self.max_total_reports = max_total_reports
639:         # Reclaims freelist pages left behind by the trims above:
640:         # DELETEs only unlink pages, so a trimming workload's file
641:         # grows to its high-water mark and stays there without VACUUM
642:         # (#39). VACUUM rewrites the whole file while holding the
643:         # write lock, so it runs at most once per `vacuum_interval`
644:         # inserts that actually deleted rows -- and even then only
645:         # when PRAGMA freelist_count shows at least
646:         # VACUUM_MIN_FREELIST_PAGES reclaimable pages. At a steady
647:         # cap (one row evicted per insert) SQLite reuses those pages
648:         # for the new rows, so there is nothing to reclaim and the
649:         # cadence hit is a no-op. 0/None disables.
650:         self.vacuum_interval = vacuum_interval
651:         self._writes_since_vacuum = 0
652:         # SQLite only ever allows one writer at a time, even in WAL mode --
653:         # under ThreadingHTTPServer, every write-handling thread opens its
654:         # own connection and would otherwise all race for that single
655:         # writer lock at once, each polling/blocking inside SQLite's own
656:         # busy_timeout. Under sustained high concurrency that busy-wait can
657:         # still lose (a real stress run: 30 threads x 300s produced 36
658:         # "database is locked" OperationalErrors past a 5s busy_timeout).
659:         # Serializing writes through this lock instead means at most one
660:         # thread ever has a write in flight against SQLite, so there is
661:         # never any lock contention for busy_timeout to time out on --
662:         # every writer just queues fairly in Python instead.
663:         self._write_lock = threading.Lock()
664:         # The DB (and its -wal/-shm siblings, recreated on every checkpoint)
665:         # hold raw report detail text, source IPs, and ban reasons -- private
666:         # regardless of the launching environment's umask, not just under the
667:         # exact systemd unit that happens to set UMask=0077. Deliberately no
668:         # os.umask() call here: umask is process-wide with no thread-local or
669:         # context-manager scoping in the stdlib, so a constructor that sets it
670:         # permanently mutates every future file creation in the importing
671:         # process (#99) -- surprising for anything using Store as a library
672:         # (tests, admin scripts). The daemon entry point (main() below) sets
673:         # a restrictive umask once at startup, before any handler thread
674:         # exists, which covers every file SQLite creates afterwards without
675:         # racing. A per-_connect() scoped umask would close the later-file
676:         # gap for library users too, but umask races process-wide under
677:         # ThreadingHTTPServer concurrency, so explicit chmod (per-file,
678:         # thread-safe) is used here instead. Normalize any pre-existing
679:         # files: an upgrade from a pre-fix deployment can already have a
680:         # world-readable DB (and -wal/-shm) on disk that sqlite3.connect()
681:         # would otherwise reuse as-is.
682:         with self._write_lock:
683:             self._ensure_private()
684:             # Validate the schema version BEFORE running any DDL: a DB
685:             # stamped with an unknown future version must be refused
686:             # without creating tables in it first. The probe is a bare
687:             # connection, not _connect() -- whose WAL upgrade would
688:             # itself persist a change to the refused file.
689:             probe = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path, timeout=5)
690:             try:
691:                 try:
692:                     cur_ver = probe.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
693:                 except Exception:
694:                     cur_ver = 0
695:             finally:
696:                 probe.close()
697:             if not isinstance(cur_ver, int):
698:                 cur_ver = 0
699:             if cur_ver != 0 and cur_ver != self.SCHEMA_VERSION:
700:                 raise RuntimeError(
701:                     "ac_server: --db schema version %d unsupported "
702:                     "(this server understands version %d) -- refusing to "
703:                     "open it" % (cur_ver, self.SCHEMA_VERSION)
704:                 )
705:             conn = self._connect()
706:             conn.execute(
707:                 """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (
708:                        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
709:                        client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
710:                        event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
711:                        detail TEXT NOT NULL,
712:                        client_ts INTEGER,
713:                        received_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
714:                        source_addr TEXT NOT NULL
715:                    )"""
716:             )
717:             conn.execute(
718:                 "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reports_client ON reports(client_id)"
719:             )
720:             conn.execute(
721:                 """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bans (
722:                        client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
723:                        reason TEXT NOT NULL,
724:                        banned_at INTEGER NOT NULL
725:                    )"""
726:             )
727:             if cur_ver == 0:
728:                 conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version=%d" % (self.SCHEMA_VERSION,))
729:             conn.commit()
730:             conn.close()
731:             # Fresh files (or -wal/-shm siblings checkpoint-created above) may
732:             # have been created under the importer's own umask when Store is
733:             # used as a library (no main() umask in effect) -- lock them down
734:             # explicitly so library use still lands at 0600 without touching
735:             # the process-wide umask to get there.
736:             self._ensure_private()

738:     def _ensure_private(self):
739:         """chmod any existing DB/-wal/-shm files to 0600. Per-file and
740:         thread-safe, unlike umask -- safe to call from __init__ (both
741:         before table creation for the upgrade case and after, for the
742:         fresh-creation-as-library case) and after writes (SQLite can
743:         recreate -wal/-shm on any checkpoint, including well after
744:         __init__ when Store is used as a library without main()'s umask).
745:         A vanishing file between the exists check and the chmod (another
746:         thread's connection checkpointing the WAL away) just means there
747:         is nothing left to lock down. A symlink is skipped rather than
748:         followed: Store.__init__ already refuses a symlinked DB path, so
749:         one appearing later is suspicious and chmod would otherwise act
750:         on the link target."""
751:         for suffix in ("", "-wal", "-shm"):
752:             path = self.db_path + suffix
753:             try:
754:                 if stat.S_ISLNK(os.lstat(path).st_mode):
755:                     continue
756:             except FileNotFoundError:
757:                 continue
758:             try:
759:                 os.chmod(path, 0o600)
760:             except FileNotFoundError:
761:                 pass

763:     def _connect(self):
764:         conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path, timeout=5)
765:         # journal_mode is persistent per database file, so re-setting WAL
766:         # on every connection (#30) just retakes the writer lock for no
767:         # effect. Query first and only upgrade when not already in WAL.
768:         # :memory: handles are excluded outright: their mode reports
769:         # "memory" and WAL is unsupported there, so upgrading would be a
770:         # wasted no-op against a handle the mode check alone can't spare.
771:         try:
772:             mode = conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0]
773:         except Exception:
774:             mode = ""
775:         if (self.db_path != ":memory:"
776:                 and (not isinstance(mode, str) or mode.lower() != "wal")):
777:             try:
778:                 conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
779:             except Exception:
780:                 pass
781:         # Explicit busy_timeout as defense-in-depth: timeout=5 above is the
782:         # Python-level busy handler, but setting the SQLite-level pragma
783:         # ensures the same 5s bound even if the connection is used via raw
784:         # sqlite3 APIs that bypass Python's wrapper. Synchronous=NORMAL is
785:         # safe in WAL mode and reduces fsync pressure under concurrent writes
786:         # without sacrificing durability guarantees needed here.
787:         try:
788:             conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
789:         except Exception:
790:             pass
791:         return conn

793:     # Cap trims run under _write_lock on every insert, so they have to be
794:     # cheap when there is nothing to evict (#90). Each finds the id of the
795:     # newest row that is over the cap -- OFFSET <cap> from the top, walked
796:     # on the rowid index (or idx_reports_client, which carries the rowid)
797:     # -- and deletes at or below it. Under the cap the subquery is NULL and
798:     # the DELETE matches nothing. The previous `id NOT IN (... LIMIT ?)`
799:     # shape kept the same rows but scanned the whole table per insert.
800:     _TRIM_CLIENT_SQL = (
801:         "DELETE FROM reports WHERE client_id = ? AND id <= ("
802:         "SELECT id FROM reports WHERE client_id = ? "
803:         "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?)"
804:     )
805:     _TRIM_GLOBAL_SQL = (
806:         "DELETE FROM reports WHERE id <= ("
807:         "SELECT id FROM reports ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?)"
808:     )

810:     def add_report(self, client_id, event_type, detail, client_ts, source_addr):
811:         # Captured here so the stored row and the webhook payload (see
812:         # _handle_report) agree on when the report landed -- calling
813:         # now_ts() again at notify time could tick over by a second.
814:         received_at = now_ts()
815:         with self._write_lock:
816:             conn = self._connect()
817:             try:
818:                 conn.execute(
819:                     "INSERT INTO reports (client_id, event_type, detail, "
820:                     "client_ts, received_at, source_addr) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
821:                     (client_id, event_type, detail, client_ts, received_at, source_addr),
822:                 )
823:                 trimmed = 0
824:                 if self.max_reports_per_client:
825:                     cur = conn.execute(
826:                         self._TRIM_CLIENT_SQL,
827:                         (client_id, client_id, self.max_reports_per_client),

829:                     trimmed += cur.rowcount
830:                 if self.max_total_reports:
831:                     cur = conn.execute(
832:                         self._TRIM_GLOBAL_SQL, (self.max_total_reports,)
833:                     )
834:                     trimmed += cur.rowcount

836:                 self._maybe_vacuum(conn, trimmed)
837:                 # SQLite may have (re)created -wal/-shm on this write; lock
838:                 # them down while the connection is still open (they exist
839:                 # now, not just at __init__ time). Harmless under the daemon
840:                 # (main()'s umask already made them 0600); what actually
841:                 # needs it is Store-as-library use with no such umask.
842:                 self._ensure_private()
843:             finally:
844:                 conn.close()

847:     def _maybe_vacuum(self, conn, trimmed):
848:         """Run VACUUM at most once per `vacuum_interval` trimming inserts,
849:         and only when enough freelist pages have actually accumulated."""
850:         # A failure here must never fail the insert it follows -- the file
851:         # just stays at its high-water mark until the next cadence hit.
852:         # Steady-state cap churn (one row evicted per insert) reuses its
853:         # own pages, so an unconditional rewrite here would block every
854:         # other writer under _write_lock to reclaim nothing, forever.
855:         if not trimmed or not self.vacuum_interval:
856:             return
857:         self._writes_since_vacuum += 1
858:         if self._writes_since_vacuum < self.vacuum_interval:
859:             return
860:         self._writes_since_vacuum = 0
861:         try:
862:             freelist = conn.execute("PRAGMA freelist_count").fetchone()[0]
863:         except Exception as e:
864:             sys.stderr.write("ac_server: freelist check failed: %r\n" % (e,))
865:             return
866:         if freelist < self.VACUUM_MIN_FREELIST_PAGES:
867:             return
868:         try:
869:             conn.execute("VACUUM")
870:         except Exception as e:
871:             sys.stderr.write("ac_server: VACUUM failed: %r\n" % (e,))

994: def _parse_socket_mode(value):
995:     """Parse --unix-socket-mode into a numeric file mode.
996:     Accepts the usual octal spellings ("0600", "600", "0o600").
997:     Raises ValueError on anything else -- main() turns that into a
998:     startup refusal. Range-checked to 0..0o777 so a typo like "06000"
999:     can't silently land somewhere unexpected."""
1000:     text = value.strip()
1001:     for prefix in ("0o", "0O"):
1002:         if text.startswith(prefix):
1003:             text = text[len(prefix):]
1004:             break
1005:     if not text or any(c not in "01234567" for c in text):
1006:         raise ValueError("invalid --unix-socket-mode %r: use an octal "
1007:                          "mode like 0600" % (value,))
1008:     mode = int(text, 8)
1009:     if mode < 0 or mode > 0o777:
1010:         raise ValueError("invalid --unix-socket-mode %r: use an octal "
1011:                          "mode between 0000 and 0777" % (value,))
1012:     return mode

492:             # O_NOFOLLOW directory fd held since the stale-path check

496:             # because the directory is required non-writable above.
497:             fd = self.socket.fileno()

500:                 os.fchmod(fd, self._socket_mode)

503:                 os.umask(old_umask)

505:             self.server_port = 0

507:                 os.chown(sock_name, -1, self._socket_gid,
508:                          dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False)

511:                 raise RuntimeError(
512:                     "ac_server: --unix-socket path %r is not a socket "
513:                     "after bind -- refusing to run" % (self.server_address,)

517:             # --unix-socket transport (see the module docstring's "No TLS"
518:             # / unix-socket note), defaulting to 0600 to match Store's
519:             # own DB-file permissions (see Store.__init__).
520:             if stat.S_IMODE(bound.st_mode) != self._socket_mode:

522:                     "ac_server: --unix-socket path %r has mode %04o after bind, "
523:                     "expected %04o -- refusing to run with unintended "
524:                     "permissions" % (self.server_address,
525:                                      stat.S_IMODE(bound.st_mode),
526:                                      self._socket_mode)
527:                 )
528:             if self._socket_gid is not None and bound.st_gid != self._socket_gid:
529:                 raise RuntimeError(
530:                     "ac_server: --unix-socket path %r has unexpected group "
531:                     "ownership after bind -- refusing to run" % (self.server_address,)
532:                 )

534:             # can confirm the path still names *this* socket before removing
535:             # it -- not, say, a replacement another process created at the
536:             # same path after this one closed it.
537:             self._bound_stat = bound

539:             os.close(dir_fd)

588: class Store:
589:     """One SQLite connection per request (see handler) -- simplest way to
590:     be correct under ThreadingHTTPServer without sharing a connection
591:     across threads."""

593:     # SQLite schema version, tracked via PRAGMA user_version (#30: the
594:     # server previously had no schema-migration/versioning story at all).
595:     # Fresh DBs are stamped with this; pre-existing version-0 DBs (every
596:     # DB created before this existed) are stamped on open since their
597:     # tables already match version 1. Anything else is a newer/unknown
598:     # schema this code doesn't understand -- fail closed rather than
599:     # writing into it.
600:     SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
601: 
602:     def __init__(self, db_path, max_reports_per_client=1000,
603:                  max_total_reports=100000, vacuum_interval=1000):
604:         self.db_path = db_path
605:         # Fail closed on a symlinked DB path (#30): sqlite3.connect()
606:         # follows symlinks, so a pre-planted link would redirect every
607:         # report/ban read and write (and the _ensure_private chmod below)
608:         # at an attacker-chosen target. Only the final component is
609:         # checked -- a symlinked parent dir (e.g. /tmp -> /private/tmp)
610:         # is a normal configuration, not an attack. The check races a
611:         # concurrent swap between lstat and connect when the DB dir is
612:         # writable by someone else; the deployment expectation (same as
613:         # the --unix-socket dir rule) is an operator-owned dir.
614:         try:
615:             st = os.lstat(db_path)
616:         except FileNotFoundError:
617:             pass
618:         else:
619:             if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
620:                 raise RuntimeError(
621:                     "ac_server: --db path %r is a symlink -- refusing to "
622:                     "open it (point --db at the real file)" % (db_path,)
623:                 )
624:         # Bounds how many rows a single client_id can hold in `reports`,
625:         # trimmed on every insert (see add_report). Without this, a single
626:         # spammy or misbehaving daemon has no limit on how much it can grow
627:         # the SQLite file, since `list_reports`'s LIMIT only bounds what a
628:         # query returns, not what accumulates on disk (#60). 0/None disables
629:         # the cap.
630:         self.max_reports_per_client = max_reports_per_client
631:         # Bounds how many rows the whole `reports` table can hold across
632:         # ALL client_ids, trimmed on every insert right after the
633:         # per-client trim above (see add_report). The per-client cap alone
634:         # can't do this: anyone able to mint arbitrarily many distinct
635:         # client_ids grows the SQLite file without bound (#26). Oldest
636:         # rows go first, same as the per-client trim. 0/None disables
637:         # the cap.
638:         self.max_total_reports = max_total_reports
639:         # Reclaims freelist pages left behind by the trims above:
640:         # DELETEs only unlink pages, so a trimming workload's file
641:         # grows to its high-water mark and stays there without VACUUM
642:         # (#39). VACUUM rewrites the whole file while holding the
643:         # write lock, so it runs at most once per `vacuum_interval`
644:         # inserts that actually deleted rows -- and even then only
645:         # when PRAGMA freelist_count shows at least
646:         # VACUUM_MIN_FREELIST_PAGES reclaimable pages. At a steady
647:         # cap (one row evicted per insert) SQLite reuses those pages
648:         # for the new rows, so there is nothing to reclaim and the
649:         # cadence hit is a no-op. 0/None disables.
650:         self.vacuum_interval = vacuum_interval
651:         self._writes_since_vacuum = 0
652:         # SQLite only ever allows one writer at a time, even in WAL mode --
653:         # under ThreadingHTTPServer, every write-handling thread opens its
654:         # own connection and would otherwise all race for that single
655:         # writer lock at once, each polling/blocking inside SQLite's own
656:         # busy_timeout. Under sustained high concurrency that busy-wait can
657:         # still lose (a real stress run: 30 threads x 300s produced 36
658:         # "database is locked" OperationalErrors past a 5s busy_timeout).
659:         # Serializing writes through this lock instead means at most one
660:         # thread ever has a write in flight against SQLite, so there is
661:         # never any lock contention for busy_timeout to time out on --
662:         # every writer just queues fairly in Python instead.
663:         self._write_lock = threading.Lock()
664:         # The DB (and its -wal/-shm siblings, recreated on every checkpoint)
665:         # hold raw report detail text, source IPs, and ban reasons -- private
666:         # regardless of the launching environment's umask, not just under the
667:         # exact systemd unit that happens to set UMask=0077. Deliberately no
668:         # os.umask() call here: umask is process-wide with no thread-local or
669:         # context-manager scoping in the stdlib, so a constructor that sets it
670:         # permanently mutates every future file creation in the importing
671:         # process (#99) -- surprising for anything using Store as a library
672:         # (tests, admin scripts). The daemon entry point (main() below) sets
673:         # a restrictive umask once at startup, before any handler thread
674:         # exists, which covers every file SQLite creates afterwards without
675:         # racing. A per-_connect() scoped umask would close the later-file
676:         # gap for library users too, but umask races process-wide under
677:         # ThreadingHTTPServer concurrency, so explicit chmod (per-file,
678:         # thread-safe) is used here instead. Normalize any pre-existing
679:         # files: an upgrade from a pre-fix deployment can already have a
680:         # world-readable DB (and -wal/-shm) on disk that sqlite3.connect()
681:         # would otherwise reuse as-is.
682:         with self._write_lock:
683:             self._ensure_private()
684:             # Validate the schema version BEFORE running any DDL: a DB
685:             # stamped with an unknown future version must be refused
686:             # without creating tables in it first. The probe is a bare
687:             # connection, not _connect() -- whose WAL upgrade would
688:             # itself persist a change to the refused file.
689:             probe = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path, timeout=5)
690:             try:
691:                 try:
692:                     cur_ver = probe.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
693:                 except Exception:
694:                     cur_ver = 0
695:             finally:
696:                 probe.close()
697:             if not isinstance(cur_ver, int):
698:                 cur_ver = 0
699:             if cur_ver != 0 and cur_ver != self.SCHEMA_VERSION:
700:                 raise RuntimeError(
701:                     "ac_server: --db schema version %d unsupported "
702:                     "(this server understands version %d) -- refusing to "
703:                     "open it" % (cur_ver, self.SCHEMA_VERSION)
704:                 )
705:             conn = self._connect()
706:             conn.execute(
707:                 """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (
708:                        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
709:                        client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
710:                        event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
711:                        detail TEXT NOT NULL,
712:                        client_ts INTEGER,
713:                        received_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
714:                        source_addr TEXT NOT NULL
715:                    )"""
716:             )
717:             conn.execute(
718:                 "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reports_client ON reports(client_id)"
719:             )
720:             conn.execute(
721:                 """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bans (
722:                        client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
723:                        reason TEXT NOT NULL,
724:                        banned_at INTEGER NOT NULL
725:                    )"""
726:             )
727:             if cur_ver == 0:
728:                 conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version=%d" % (self.SCHEMA_VERSION,))
729:             conn.commit()
730:             conn.close()
731:             # Fresh files (or -wal/-shm siblings checkpoint-created above) may
732:             # have been created under the importer's own umask when Store is
733:             # used as a library (no main() umask in effect) -- lock them down
734:             # explicitly so library use still lands at 0600 without touching
735:             # the process-wide umask to get there.
736:             self._ensure_private()
737: 
738:     def _ensure_private(self):
739:         """chmod any existing DB/-wal/-shm files to 0600. Per-file and
740:         thread-safe, unlike umask -- safe to call from __init__ (both
741:         before table creation for the upgrade case and after, for the
742:         fresh-creation-as-library case) and after writes (SQLite can
743:         recreate -wal/-shm on any checkpoint, including well after
744:         __init__ when Store is used as a library without main()'s umask).
745:         A vanishing file between the exists check and the chmod (another
746:         thread's connection checkpointing the WAL away) just means there
747:         is nothing left to lock down. A symlink is skipped rather than
748:         followed: Store.__init__ already refuses a symlinked DB path, so
749:         one appearing later is suspicious and chmod would otherwise act
750:         on the link target."""
751:         for suffix in ("", "-wal", "-shm"):
752:             path = self.db_path + suffix
753:             try:
754:                 if stat.S_ISLNK(os.lstat(path).st_mode):
755:                     continue
756:             except FileNotFoundError:
757:                 continue
758:             try:
759:                 os.chmod(path, 0o600)
760:             except FileNotFoundError:
761:                 pass

763:     def _connect(self):
764:         conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path, timeout=5)
765:         # journal_mode is persistent per database file, so re-setting WAL
766:         # on every connection (#30) just retakes the writer lock for no
767:         # effect. Query first and only upgrade when not already in WAL.
768:         # :memory: handles are excluded outright: their mode reports
769:         # "memory" and WAL is unsupported there, so upgrading would be a
770:         # wasted no-op against a handle the mode check alone can't spare.
771:         try:
772:             mode = conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0]
773:         except Exception:
774:             mode = ""
775:         if (self.db_path != ":memory:"
776:                 and (not isinstance(mode, str) or mode.lower() != "wal")):
777:             try:
778:                 conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
779:             except Exception:
780:                 pass
781:         # Explicit busy_timeout as defense-in-depth: timeout=5 above is the
782:         # Python-level busy handler, but setting the SQLite-level pragma
783:         # ensures the same 5s bound even if the connection is used via raw
784:         # sqlite3 APIs that bypass Python's wrapper. Synchronous=NORMAL is
785:         # safe in WAL mode and reduces fsync pressure under concurrent writes
786:         # without sacrificing durability guarantees needed here.
787:         try:
788:             conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
789:         except Exception:
790:             pass
791:         return conn

793:     # Cap trims run under _write_lock on every insert, so they have to be
794:     # cheap when there is nothing to evict (#90). Each finds the id of the
795:     # newest row that is over the cap -- OFFSET <cap> from the top, walked
796:     # on the rowid index (or idx_reports_client, which carries the rowid)
797:     # -- and deletes at or below it. Under the cap the subquery is NULL and
798:     # the DELETE matches nothing. The previous `id NOT IN (... LIMIT ?)`
799:     # shape kept the same rows but scanned the whole table per insert.
800:     _TRIM_CLIENT_SQL = (
801:         "DELETE FROM reports WHERE client_id = ? AND id <= ("
802:         "SELECT id FROM reports WHERE client_id = ? "
803:         "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?)"
804:     )
805:     _TRIM_GLOBAL_SQL = (
806:         "DELETE FROM reports WHERE id <= ("
807:         "SELECT id FROM reports ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?)"
808:     )

810:     def add_report(self, client_id, event_type, detail, client_ts, source_addr):
811:         # Captured here so the stored row and the webhook payload (see
812:         # _handle_report) agree on when the report landed -- calling
813:         # now_ts() again at notify time could tick over by a second.
814:         received_at = now_ts()
815:         with self._write_lock:
816:             conn = self._connect()
817:             try:
818:                 conn.execute(
819:                     "INSERT INTO reports (client_id, event_type, detail, "
820:                     "client_ts, received_at, source_addr) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
821:                     (client_id, event_type, detail, client_ts, received_at, source_addr),
822:                 )
823:                 trimmed = 0
824:                 if self.max_reports_per_client:
825:                     cur = conn.execute(
826:                         self._TRIM_CLIENT_SQL,
827:                         (client_id, client_id, self.max_reports_per_client),
828:                     )
829:                     trimmed += cur.rowcount
830:                 if self.max_total_reports:
831:                     cur = conn.execute(
832:                         self._TRIM_GLOBAL_SQL, (self.max_total_reports,)
833:                     )
834:                     trimmed += cur.rowcount
835:                 conn.commit()
836:                 self._maybe_vacuum(conn, trimmed)
837:                 # SQLite may have (re)created -wal/-shm on this write; lock
838:                 # them down while the connection is still open (they exist
839:                 # now, not just at __init__ time). Harmless under the daemon
840:                 # (main()'s umask already made them 0600); what actually
841:                 # needs it is Store-as-library use with no such umask.
842:                 self._ensure_private()
843:             finally:
844:                 conn.close()
845:         return received_at

847:     def _maybe_vacuum(self, conn, trimmed):
848:         """Run VACUUM at most once per `vacuum_interval` trimming inserts,
849:         and only when enough freelist pages have actually accumulated."""
850:         # A failure here must never fail the insert it follows -- the file
851:         # just stays at its high-water mark until the next cadence hit.
852:         # Steady-state cap churn (one row evicted per insert) reuses its
853:         # own pages, so an unconditional rewrite here would block every
854:         # other writer under _write_lock to reclaim nothing, forever.
855:         if not trimmed or not self.vacuum_interval:
856:             return
857:         self._writes_since_vacuum += 1
858:         if self._writes_since_vacuum < self.vacuum_interval:
859:             return
860:         self._writes_since_vacuum = 0
861:         try:
862:             freelist = conn.execute("PRAGMA freelist_count").fetchone()[0]
863:         except Exception as e:
864:             sys.stderr.write("ac_server: freelist check failed: %r\n" % (e,))
865:             return
866:         if freelist < self.VACUUM_MIN_FREELIST_PAGES:
867:             return
868:         try:
869:             conn.execute("VACUUM")
870:         except Exception as e:
871:             sys.stderr.write("ac_server: VACUUM failed: %r\n" % (e,))

994: def _parse_socket_mode(value):
995:     """Parse --unix-socket-mode into a numeric file mode.
996:     Accepts the usual octal spellings ("0600", "600", "0o600").
997:     Raises ValueError on anything else -- main() turns that into a
998:     startup refusal. Range-checked to 0..0o777 so a typo like "06000"
999:     can't silently land somewhere unexpected."""
1000:     text = value.strip()
1001:     for prefix in ("0o", "0O"):
1002:         if text.startswith(prefix):
1003:             text = text[len(prefix):]
1004:             break
1005:     if not text or any(c not in "01234567" for c in text):
